key_insight: SEM-DNN identifies bidirectional contemporaneous causal effects by forcing the conditional residual covariance of a heteroscedastic neural simultaneous-equation model to diagonalize across covariates.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to estimate feedback loops in autonomous systems from observational data when external instruments are unavailable, enabling more faithful structural modeling and intervention analysis.
method: Neural simultaneous equations model nonlinear structural means and feature-dependent variances.
Uses diagonal Gaussian quasi-likelihood with the simultaneous-system Jacobian.
Identification comes from conditional covariance diagonalization under nonproportional variances and zero-mean, conditionally uncorrelated shocks.
evidence_signal: Monte Carlo tests with nonlinear, high-dimensional nuisance functions and non-Gaussian shocks show better recovery of structural effects than parametric, kernel, and separate-equation neural baselines, and a cereal scanner-data case study examines price-sales feedback and identification diagnostics.
watch_item: Performance comes with higher computational cost, and results may be sensitive to optimization stability, variance calibration, and whether the neural parametrization satisfies the required profile-compatibility conditions.
paper_title: Learning Bidirectional Causal Interactions with Heteroscedastic Neural Networks
